content.text:
Review the STAGED diff in this worktree (`git diff --cached`). It is PR A1 of an ACL hardening change. Read the surrounding code before asserting anything.

## What it is trying to do
`member_of` is simultaneously an ACL primitive and ordinary domain vocabulary. `ensureMemberOfType` upserts on (organization_id, slug) — it ADOPTS a pre-existing row rather than create-or-failing — so an org defining `member_of` in its own `lobu apply` schema would have that type silently promoted into the access path.

This PR adds a system-controlled `purpose='authorization'` classification, stamps it on the ACL type (repairing on adopt), and refuses caller mutation of any classified type.

Deliberately NOT in this PR: the three ACL read predicates (`AND rt.purpose='authorization'` in channel-visibility.ts, resource-visibility.ts, channel-messages-visibility.ts). They ship in a follow-up so a rolling deploy cannot have new readers demanding a stamp that old pods are not yet writing.

## Verify specifically
1. Is the guard set COMPLETE? Find any remaining path by which a caller (not the platform ACL syncs) can create, modify, soft-delete, or otherwise influence an edge on a classified type, or change/archive/rename the classified type itself. Include the CLI/apply path, any HTTP route, MCP surfaces, bulk/import paths, and entity merge. Name file:line.
2. Is `assertNotAuthorizationType` placed at genuine chokepoints, or can a handler reach the mutation without passing it?
3. Does the `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.purpose, entity_relationship_types.purpose)` upsert have a failure mode? Consider `mentions` and `member_of` sharing `ensureRelationshipType`, and the archived/status='active' partial index.
4. Is the migration safe? It classifies ALL active `member_of` rows. Consider public/cross-org visibility types, archived rows, and orgs where `member_of` was created by apply rather than the platform.
5. Does the two-deploy split actually remove the rolling-deploy hazard, or is there still a window?
6. Anything in the tests that passes for the wrong reason, or a guard asserted only via the helper rather than the real surface.

Be concrete and cite file:line. Rank by severity. If something is fine, say so briefly rather than padding.

I’ll use the Lobu operator skill because this is a staged monorepo security review with repo-specific gates and mutation boundaries. I’ll first load its instructions and relevant prior ACL/schema context, then trace every write surface from public handlers down to the staged chokepoints.

content.text:
Verdict: not complete. The staged guard set still has three high-severity and two medium-severity gaps.

## Findings

1. High — Entity merge, unmerge, and deletion bypass the classified-edge guard.

`manage_entity` exposes delete/merge/unmerge at [manage_entity.ts:192](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:192) and [manage_entity.ts:207](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:207), but none checks relationship-type purpose.

- Merge loads every live edge touching the loser, regardless of purpose, then tombstones collisions and repoints the survivors at [entity-merge.ts:230](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:230), [entity-merge.ts:298](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:298), and [entity-merge.ts:327](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/acl-purpose-classification/packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts:327). Merging two member entities can transfer one person’s channel grants to another.
